key_insight: An AI-assisted digital workflow for tissue-based autoantibody interpretation improved accuracy and consistency in autoimmune encephalitis screening, especially for less-experienced readers.
clinical_relevance: This could help laboratories reduce reader-dependent variability and improve confidence in neural autoantibody testing, supporting more reliable diagnostic workflows.
method: Trained on 2,357 retrospective serum and CSF tissue-based assay images from >80 institutions
Validated prospectively on 200 unique-patient images with expert consensus reference labels
Compared unaided vs AI-assisted interpretation by two experts and two novices in a two-round reader study
evidence_signal: In prospective validation, the standalone classifier reached AUROC 0.922 with 86.5% accuracy, and AI assistance raised pooled reader accuracy from 90.4% to 97.4% (McNemar P < 0.001).
watch_item: Results came from centralized, expert-reviewed images in a single workflow, so broader multicenter and cross-platform validation is still needed before routine deployment.
paper_title: AI-Assisted Tissue-Based Antibody Interpretation in Autoimmune Encephalitis: Prospective Validation and Reader Study
